clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: the order exempts the employee 'until December 1, 1936'. Recorded as 1936-12-01, inclusive (runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the exclusive alternative ends the exemption when that day began. Actor: EO 7232 itself.

research_rationale:
EO 7232 (November 23, 1935, Franklin D. Roosevelt). Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming EO 7232, its date (November 23, 1935) appears in the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. It exempts Frederick D. Henry, Chief Clerk, Freedmen's Hospital, Department of the Interior from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until December 1, 1936. Identity: number, date, person and end date agree across the APP page, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1936-12-01, inclusive. Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) census titles in jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv with retirement wording for the surname; (2) every WPA 1944 numbered-list entry (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, whitespace-insensitive) for the surname with retirement wording; (3) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts and jobs/*/data for the person's full name within reach of 'retire' or 'exempt'; (4) a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 7232' and list forms ('Orders Nos. ... 7232'). They found no later order naming this employee. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 through and after this date (EO 7725 of October 12, 1937, running to November 1, 1938, and EO 7842 of March 15, 1938, running to June 1, 1939), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.

The employee's death or separation before the date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, an end of the order, and no held record shows such an event.
